header: THE REFUNDABLE PF LOAN OF DSP: the monthly instalment (EMI), the interest, the month-by-month schedule and the yearly summary. This file is pure: what a person types is used in the browser and is never stored, logged or sent. DSP has two kinds of PF loan: the NON-REFUNDABLE one (NRL), which is not paid back (the PF page shows it as "Less N.R.Loan"), so it has no instalment; and the REFUNDABLE one, which this file works out. THE THREE RULES of the refundable loan, as the HOD of C&IT gave them:
1. the loan's interest is always 1 percentage point more than the interest the PF deposit earns (8.25% on the deposit gives 9.25% on the loan);

2. the period is at most 10 years, and never longer than the employee's service still to run (the loan has to be paid back before retirement: "provided the employee has equal or more length of service");
3. the interest is worked on the balance that is still owed, month by month (reducing balance), in equal monthly instalments.

I do not check here how much an employee may borrow, and the screen says so: that is for the PF rules and the trust to decide. The deposit rate is an input with a default (it is declared each year), not a hidden constant. I count the service left in whole months from the current month to the month of retirement, the retirement month included (the instalment is taken from that month's pay as well, as its PF contribution is).

symbols.name: loanRatePct
doc: Returns the loan's yearly rate in percent for a deposit rate in percent; it is always one point more.

symbols.name: monthsOfService
symbols.sig: const monthsOfService = (retire: YMD, today: YMD): number =>
doc: Whole months from the current month to the month of retirement, the retirement month included (0 or less means no service left to repay in).

members.name: maxMonths
doc: The longest period this employee may take, in months.

members.name: bound
doc: What sets the limit: the ten years of the rule, or the service left.

symbols.name: tenureLimit
symbols.sig: export function tenureLimit(retire: YMD | null, today: YMD): TenureLimit | Problem
doc: The longest period for an employee who retires on that date: 10 years, or the service left if that is less; or a problem when there is no service left.

symbols.name: pfLoanEmi
symbols.sig: export function pfLoanEmi(i: PfLoanInput): PfLoanResult | Problem

behaviours: the loan's rate is the deposit's rate plus 1 point: 8.25 -> 9.25, 8 -> 9, 7.1 -> 8.1, 0 -> 1
the form's default deposit rate is the PF page's rate, 8.25, so the loan starts at 9.25
the loan is worked at the deposit's rate plus one: 8.25 gives 9.25, and the result says both
a different deposit rate moves the loan's rate with it (9%: 10%), and the EMI changes
EMI of 10 lakh at 9.25% for 10 years is 12,803.27 (worked separately); for 5 years 20,879.90
the total interest is the instalments less the loan: 5,36,392.66
the first month's interest is a month of 9.25% on the WHOLE loan (the balance owed)
each month's interest is on the balance that is left (it falls month by month), and principal + interest is the EMI in every month but the last
the schedule has one row for each month and ends at exactly zero
the yearly rows add up to the schedule: 10 years, principal 10 lakh, balance zero at the end
part of a year at the end gives one more yearly row (30 months: 3 rows)
months of service: Nov 2026 to Mar 2032 is 64 (Dec 2026 to Mar 2032, the retirement month included); to Mar 2040 is 160
with more than 10 years to go the limit is 120 months, set by the ten years
with 64 months to go the limit is 64, set by the service left
exactly 10 years of service left is allowed: 120 months
10 years exactly is allowed; 121 months is refused with the rule
a period equal to the service left is allowed (64 months with 64 left); one month more is refused and says how much service is left
10 years with 9 years of service left is refused (service, not the ten years, is the limit)
no retirement date: nothing is calculated, and it asks for the date (the rule needs it)
a retirement this month or past: no service left to repay in
impossible figures are told: no amount, a negative rate, a rate over 30, a fraction of a month, zero months
a loan with a zero deposit rate carries 1%, not zero
the same inputs always give the same answer (pure)
